basis_documents: Revised Section F: Natural Products and Related Compounds, IUPAC Recommendations 1999
value.source_text: This Section is based on the recent publication ‘Revised Section F: Natural Products and Related Compounds, IUPAC Recommendations 1999’ and the additional document ‘Corrections and Modifications 2004’ (ref. 9).

value.condition: a compound is isolated from a natural source and a trivial name is required
value.source_material: the biological material from which the compound was isolated
value.source_text: P-101.1.1 When a compound is isolated from a natural source and a trivial name is required, the name should be based, whenever possible, on the family, genus, or species name of the biological material from which it has been isolated.

value.condition: the compound occurs in a number of related families and use is appropriate
value.source_text: If appropriate, the class or order might also be used for the name of a compound that occurs in a number of related families.

value.condition: the trivial name describes a compound of unknown structure
value.source_text: P-101.1.2 The ending ‘une’ or, for euphonic reasons, ‘iune’ is used to indicate that the trivial name it terminates describes a compound of unknown structure.

value.class_characterization: a set of closely related parent structures
value.derivation_basis: one or more defined operations used in systematic substitutive nomenclature
value.source_text: Many naturally occurring compounds belong to well defined structural classes, each of which can be characterized by a set of parent structures that are closely related structurally, that is, each can be derived from a fundamental parent structure by one or more defined operations used in systematic substitutive nomenclature (see P-13).

value.basis: Rules prescribed in Chapters P-1 through P-9
value.source_text: As soon as the structure of a simple new natural product has been fully determined, the trivial name should be abandoned in favor of a systematic name formed by the Rules prescribed in Chapters P-1 through P-9 for systematic nomenclature of organic compounds.
For a more complicated structure, an existing semisystematic name listed in P-101.2.7 is used to fully name the compound.

value.action: form and number a new parent structure
value.condition: no previously known parent structure can be found
value.source_text: If a previously known parent structure cannot be found, a new parent structure is formed and numbered as follows.

value.application: formation and numbering of a new parent structure
value.procedure: the procedure described in the following subsections
value.source_text: To form and number a new parent structure, the procedure described in the following subsections is followed.

value.criterion: reflect the basic skeleton common to most compounds of the class
value.source_text: P-101.2.1.1 A fundamental parent structure should reflect the basic skeleton (including nonterminal heteroatoms and hetero groups) that is common to most compounds of the class.

value.criterion: maximize the natural products derivable from each parent structure
value.derivation_method: well defined operations and rules of organic nomenclature
value.source_text: P-101.2.1.2 Fundamental parent structures should be chosen so that as many natural products as possible can be derived from each by well defined operations and rules of the nomenclature of organic compounds.

value.criterion: include as much common configuration as possible
value.scope: the relevant class of natural products
value.source_text: P-101.2.1.3 A fundamental parent structure should include as much configuration as possible that is common to the relevant class of natural products.

value.refers_to: fundamental parent structures containing common configuration
value.source_text: Such parent structures are called ‘stereoparents’.
The following rules are applicable to new parent structures.

value.condition: existing parent structure name does not follow the new rules
value.source_text: Existing parent structure names are considered as retained names if they do not follow the new rules (see Table 10.1).

value.exceptional_inclusion: rings that are part of a characteristic group
value.source_text: P-101.2.2.1 A fundamental parent structure should exceptionally include rings that are part of a characteristic group, such as a lactone or cyclic acetal.
P-101.2.2.2 A fundamental parent structure should not contain terminal heteroatoms or characteristic groups (see P-101.2.1.1).

value.frequency_condition: occur in most compounds in the natural product class
value.source_text: P-101.2.2.3 A fundamental parent structure should contain acyclic hydrocarbon groups that occur in most of the compounds in the natural product class.

value.constraint: represent the saturation or unsaturation level of as many related compounds as possible
value.objective: choose a nearly fully saturated or fully unsaturated parent structure
value.source_text: P-101.2.2.4 A fundamental parent structure should be as nearly fully saturated or fully unsaturated in terms of maximum number of noncumulative double bonds (mancude rings), while still representing the level of saturation (or unsaturation) of as many related compounds as possible.
value.unsaturation_measure: maximum number of noncumulative double bonds in mancude rings

value.derivation_basis: a trivial name formed in accordance with P-101
value.source_text: P-101.2.2.5 A semisystematic name for a fundamental parent structure should be derived, as far as possible, from a trivial name formed in accordance with P-101.

value.assignment: select the applicable ending from the following ordered cases
value.operation: replace the unknown-structure ending une or iune
value.source_text: The endings to be used in place of ‘une’ or ‘iune’ must be assigned as follows:

value.condition: the entire stereoparent hydride is fully saturated
value.source_text: (a) ‘ane’, if the entire stereoparent hydride is fully saturated;

value.condition: the cyclic or the main chain of the acyclic part contains the maximum number of noncumulative double bonds
value.source_text: (b) ‘ene’, if the cyclic or the main chain of the acyclic part contains the maximum number of noncumulative double bonds;

value.condition: an otherwise fully saturated parent structure contains one or more individual mancude rings
value.source_text: (c) ‘arane’, if, in an otherwise fully saturated parent structure, one or more individual mancude rings is present.

value.condition: ending differs from the indicated endings
value.source_text: Existing names of parent structures in which endings are different from those indicated above, for example morphinan and ibogamine, are exceptions and treated as retained names.

value.purpose: describe isomers of fundamental parent structures
value.source_text: P-101.2.2.6 Indicated hydrogen, as defined in P-14.7, P-25.7 and P-58.2, is used to describe isomers of fundamental parent structures.

value.action: use the established pattern to number the fundamental parent structure
value.condition: a numbering pattern is established among structurally related natural products
value.requirement: all skeletal atoms are included in the numbering system
value.source_text: P-101.2.3.1 A numbering pattern established among a group of structurally related natural products is used for numbering the skeletal atoms of the fundamental parent structure, providing that all skeletal atoms have been included in the numbering system.

value.condition: no numbering pattern is established among structurally related natural products
value.source_text: P-101.2.3.2 If no numbering pattern has been become established among the members of a group of structurally related natural products, the fundamental parent structure is numbered according to the following guidelines:

value.action: examine the skeleton to identify the senior ring or ring system
value.source_text: (a) examine the skeleton to identify the senior ring or ring system, according to P-44.
The locant ‘1’ is assigned to the atom of the senior ring system whose locant would be ‘1’ according to systematic numbering for that particular ring or ring system;
value.target: the atom of the senior ring system whose locant would be 1 according to systematic numbering for that particular ring or ring system

value.action: assign all skeletal atoms of the senior ring system consecutive Arabic numbers
value.includes: atoms of fusion positions in fused ring systems
value.path: the path prescribed for that particular type of ring or ring system
value.source_text: (b) assign all skeletal atoms of the senior ring system consecutive Arabic numbers, including atoms of fusion positions in fused ring systems, beginning with the locant ‘1’, and following the path prescribed for that particular type of ring or ring system;

value.action: number acyclic substituents to skeletal atoms of ring components or connecting acyclic structures each in its entirety
value.order_basis: increasing value of the locant of the skeletal atom to which it is attached
value.source_text: (c) number acyclic substituents to skeletal atoms of ring components or connecting acyclic structures each in its entirety, including branches, in order of the increasing value of the locant of the skeletal atom to which it is attached;

value.action: number skeletal atoms of acyclic connections to other ring or ring systems consecutively
value.source_text: (d) number skeletal atoms of acyclic connections to other ring or ring systems, if any, consecutively beginning with the atom next to the senior ring system, followed by the skeletal atoms of the other rings or ring systems as prescribed in (b) above;
value.start: the atom next to the senior ring system
value.then: the skeletal atoms of the other rings or ring systems as prescribed in step (b)

value.condition: two or more acyclic connections to other rings or ring systems are present
value.order_basis: lowest numbered attachment position on the senior ring or ring system
sequence: acyclic connector at the next lower position
value.source_text: if two or more acyclic connections to other rings or ring systems are present, the one attached to the senior ring or ring system at the lowest numbered position is numbered first, then the ring attached to it, followed by the acyclic connector at the next lower position of the senior ring or ring system, etc.;

value.condition: two groups at a geminal disubstituted position
value.priority: larger group in terms of number of skeletal atoms
value.source_text: (e) number the larger group, in terms of the number of skeletal atoms, between two groups at a geminal disubstituted position first;
if there is still a choice, alphanumerical order is followed (Rule P-14.5).

value.condition: the two groups are identical and attached to a properly drawn stereoparent structure
value.source_text: If the two groups are then identical and attached to a stereoparent structure properly drawn (see Appendix 3), the group that is stereochemically ‘α’ (according to P-101.2.6) is numbered first;
value.tie_breaker: the group that is stereochemically α is numbered first

value.condition: the two groups are identical and attached to an acyclic terminal double bond
value.source_text: if the two groups are identical and attached to an acyclic terminal double bond, the group ‘trans’ to the main chain is numbered first, as described in the carotenoid recommendations (Rule 12.4 in ref. 40).
value.tie_breaker: the group trans to the main chain is numbered first

value.not_recommended: identification of individual rings by letters A, B, C, etc.
value.source_text: Since locants are used to describe skeletal modifications, as indicated in P-101.3, the identification of individual rings by letters A, B, C, etc., used in the past is no longer recommended, except for the rather special case of the removal of a terminal ring (see P-101.3.6).

value.continuity_use: names using letters to identify rings may be given where appropriate
value.source_text: Nevertheless, to provide continuity with the use of this system, names using letters to identify rings are given where appropriate, but are no longer recommended.

value.context: additive or subtractive operations modifying a fundamental parent structure
value.source_text: For nomenclature purposes, the fundamental parent structures are described by specific arrangements of atoms or groups of atoms called ‘atomic connectors’, ‘terminal segments’ and ‘bond connectors’, that must be taken into consideration in accordance with the additive or subtractive operations modifying a fundamental parent structure.

value.composition: a chain of homogeneous skeletal atoms of the same element
connects: substituted skeletal atoms in a parent structure
value.source_text: An ‘atomic connector’ is a chain of homogeneous skeletal atoms of the same element connecting any combination of bridgehead or ring junction atoms, rings, or ring systems (i.e. ring assemblies), substituted skeletal atoms in parent structure, or heteroatoms.

value.composition: an acyclic portion of homogeneous skeletal atoms
value.source_text: A ‘terminal segment’ of a skeletal structure is an acyclic portion of homogeneous skeletal atoms connected at only one end by the features of structure that terminate atomic connectors.
value.termination: features of structure that terminate atomic connectors

value.source_text: A ‘bond connector’ is a connection between any combination of bridgehead or ring junction atoms, rings, or ring systems (i.e. ring assemblies), substituted skeletal atoms, or heteroatoms.
The structures below illustrate atomic connectors, bond connectors, and terminal segments.
The use of these terms is further illustrated in P-101.3.1 in relation to the removal of skeletal atoms denoted by the prefix ‘nor’.

value.layout: one empty data cell spans both table columns

implies: absolute configuration of all chirality centers
configuration of double bonds when applicable
value.source_text: The name of a fundamental parent structure usually implies the absolute configuration of all chirality centers and the configuration of double bonds, when applicable, without further specification.

projection.alpha: attached atom or group lies below the plane of the paper
projection.beta: attached atom or group lies above the plane of the paper

value.source_text: All chirality must be defined so that for example with a steroid the stereochemistry at ‘C-5’, when relevant, is indicated by α, β or ξ. When a planar or quasi planar system of rings is denoted as a projection, as in this recommendation, an atom or group attached to the ring is called ‘α’ if it lies below or ‘β’ if it lies above the plane of the paper.

value.basis: Appendix 3 and examples used to exemplify the various rules
value.requirement: use the orientations of structure given in the rule examples and Appendix 3
value.source_text: Use of this system requires the orientations of structure as given in the examples used to exemplify the various rules and in Appendix 3.

value.position: before the name of the fundamental parent structure
value.source_text: The stereodescriptors ‘α’, ‘β’, and ‘ξ’ used to describe implicit or indicated configuration are cited before the name of the fundamental parent structure without parentheses.

value.purpose: express different aspects of the configuration of modified fundamental parent structures
value.source_text: The ‘α/β’ symbolism is used as defined above and extended in the following way to express different aspects of the configuration of modified fundamental parent structures.
